international.title: Lack of early border controls made UK ‘extremely vulnerable’ to Covid, inquiry finds
international.summary: Latest report also says test and trace failures allowed virus to spread quickly and unchecked UK politics live – latest updates The lack of international border controls at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic left the UK in an “extremely vulnerable position”, an inquiry has concluded. In the latest report from the Covid-19 inquiry, the chair, Heather Hallett, also said failures to quickly introduce a test-and-trace system allowed the virus to spread “with deadly speed across the country, virtually unchecked”.
